summary.en: Germany grows no cacao, but it is one of Europe's leading cocoa processors and chocolate makers, and most of its cocoa arrives through the Port of Hamburg. Chocolate reached Germany in the 17th century. A Dutch-run coffee house in Bremen served it in 1673. The first factory was Halloren in Halle, founded in 1804. desc.tr: Dominosteine, 1936'da Dresdenli çikolatacı Herbert Wendler'in lüks pralinlere ucuz bir alternatif olarak yarattığı, çikolata kaplı kurabiye, jöle ve marzipan katmanlı bir kış şekerlemesidir.
desc.en: Dominosteine are a winter confection of chocolate-coated layers of gingerbread, jelly and marzipan. Dresden chocolatier Herbert Wendler created them in 1936 as a cheaper alternative to luxury pralines.

desc.tr: Noel pazarlarının simgesi olan Nürnberg Lebkuchen'i ve Aachen Printen'i sıklıkla bitter ya da sütlü çikolata ile kaplanır. Köln'de Stollwerck da 1860'tan itibaren Printen üretmiştir.
desc.en: Nuremberg Lebkuchen and Aachen Printen, both Christmas-market staples, are often coated in dark or milk chocolate. Stollwerck in Cologne was also making Printen by 1860.

styles.name: Marzipan ve çikolata / Marzipan and chocolate

desc.tr: Lübeck merkezli marzipan geleneği, bitter çikolata kaplı ekmekler, patatesler ve pralinlerle çikolata kültürüyle iç içedir.
desc.en: The marzipan tradition centred on Lübeck is closely tied to chocolate. It appears as dark-chocolate-covered loaves, potatoes and pralines.
